card.name: Punctuation before an assignment or instruction
card.fires_on: Punctuation (period, comma, semicolon, question mark) or a linking word that ends a clause just before an instruction begins, such as a school writing task or a recipe or monitoring step.

modes.label: Classroom assignment
modes.description: Sentence-ending mark right before a task such as write an essay or letter.
modes.example: Use the Internet to research the snakehead fish<<.>> In your Science Journal, write an essay

modes.label: Comma after a condition
modes.description: Comma after a patient condition, before an added clause or instruction.
modes.example: Monitor patients with biliary tract disease<<,>> including acute pancreatitis, for worsening symptoms

modes.label: Procedure step
modes.description: Punctuation or small word within a lab or cooking step, before the next action.

card.writes: It slightly favors words for preparing or proceeding, such as prepare and proceed, as the next step.
card.plain: It marks the point where a sentence ends and a task or next step is about to be given.
